top_story.headline: Khanna and Massie file a war powers resolution on Yemen
top_story.dek: A bipartisan pair wants the House to order U.S. forces out of unauthorized hostilities against the Houthis.
paragraphs: On Friday, October 9, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) introduced H.Con.Res. 124, which would direct the President under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that Congress has not authorized. It was referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

Rep. Thomas Massie is listed in the Congressional Record as a cosponsor. The resolution was one of 31 bills and resolutions introduced during a House session that lasted about two minutes, and the Congressional Record shows no debate or vote on it.

sections.headline: Brief sessions in both chambers, 31 measures introduced in the House
paragraphs: Both chambers met briefly on Friday, October 9, and no votes are recorded. The House convened at 12:30 p.m. and adjourned at 12:32 p.m. until 1:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13. The Senate met at 1:30 p.m., adjourned about 40 seconds later, and returns at 3:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13.

The House introductions include the Khanna–Massie war powers resolution on Yemen, a proposal from Rep. Tom Barrett to create a White House office on artificial intelligence threats, and Rep. Michael A. Rulli’s bill to cut off federal funds to governments that celebrate Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day. The House also received a quarterly report of foreign travel expenditures, including an August congressional delegation trip to South Africa totaling $15,288.16 for eight travelers. All 31 measures follow, with none omitted.

items: H.R. 10768, sponsored by Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI-7) — would create an Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10769, sponsored by Rep. Everton Blair (D-GA-13) — would let certain facilities be placed within the right-of-way of any federally aided highway (Transportation and Infrastructure).
H.R. 10770, sponsored by Rep. Robert P. Bresnahan (R-PA-8) — would temporarily limit the use of rebates under the 340B drug discount program (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10771, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — would create an emergency preparedness grant program for higher education institutions (Transportation and Infrastructure).
H.R. 10772, sponsored by Rep. Jim Costa (D-CA-21) — would evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies (Armed Services).
H.R. 10773, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Crank (R-CO-5) — would amend the tax code to prevent governmental interference in the operation of private and religious schools (Ways and Means).

H.R. 10774, sponsored by Rep. Suzan K. DelBene (D-WA-1) — would prohibit the taking, importation, exportation and breeding of certain cetaceans for public display by amending the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 and the Animal Welfare Act (Natural Resources, with Agriculture also receiving it).

H.R. 10775, sponsored by Rep. Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA-10) — would direct the Federal Trade Commission to set up a task force studying the effects of automated accounts on social media, public discourse and elections (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10776, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) — would change requirements for allowed take of marine mammals under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 (Natural Resources).

H.R. 10777, sponsored by Rep. Pat Fallon (R-TX-4) — would codify certain policies to combat transnational cyber-enabled crime (Judiciary, with Homeland Security and Foreign Affairs also receiving it).
H.R. 10778, sponsored by Rep. Valerie P. Foushee (D-NC-4) — would create a tax credit for health care facilities that use certain low-emission anesthetic gases (Ways and Means).

H.R. 10779, sponsored by Rep. Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY-2) — would name the Postal Service facility at 1905 Route 112 in Medford, New York, the “Gunnery Sergeant Ruben Santos Post Office Building” (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.R. 10780, sponsored by Rep. Jared F. Golden (D-ME-2) — would modify and enhance the federal budgeting and appropriations process (Rules, with Budget, House Administration, Appropriations, and Oversight and Government Reform also receiving it).
H.R. 10781, sponsored by Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL-8) — would ask the President to designate a month each year as National American History and Founders Month (Judiciary).
H.R. 10782, sponsored by Rep. Jahana Hayes (D-CT-5) — would reauthorize the Clean School Bus Program (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10783, sponsored by Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC-1) — would provide for attorney’s fees to be paid to a prevailing defendant in a civil defamation or libel action (Judiciary).
H.R. 10784, sponsored by Rep. Richard McCormick (R-GA-7) — would amend the tax code to provide home ownership assistance (Ways and Means, with Financial Services also receiving it).
H.R. 10785, sponsored by Rep. Analilia Mejia (D-NJ-11) — would reauthorize the SCORE small-business mentoring program under the Small Business Act (Small Business).

H.R. 10786, sponsored by Rep. Max L. Miller (R-OH-7) — would require certain colleges to make students who are United States citizens pass the United States naturalization test in order to graduate (Education and Workforce).

H.R. 10787, sponsored by Rep. Gregory F. Murphy (R-NC-3) — would exclude urological and ostomy supplies from Medicare competitive acquisition programs for five years (Energy and Commerce, with Ways and Means also receiving it).

H.R. 10788, sponsored by Rep. Frank Pallone (D-NJ-6) — — titled the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act — would adjust the surprise medical billing requirements for private health insurance (Energy and Commerce, with Education and Workforce and Ways and Means also receiving it).
H.R. 10789, sponsored by Rep. Jimmy Patronis (R-FL-1) — would establish a moratorium on oil and gas production and exploration in the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range (Natural Resources).

H.R. 10790, sponsored by Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-WA-3) — would require that at least one member of the Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board have demonstrated knowledge and substantial experience in the trades or industrial labor (Energy and Commerce).

H.R. 10791, sponsored by Rep. Michael A. Rulli (R-OH-6) — would bar federal funds to any state or local government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.R. 10792, sponsored by Rep. Janice D. Schakowsky (D-IL-9) — would provide incentives for and protect whistleblowers under the authority of the Federal Trade Commission (Education and Workforce, with Energy and Commerce also receiving it).
H.R. 10793, sponsored by Rep. Derek Schmidt (R-KS-2) — would modify Department of Defense authority for installation support services and intergovernmental support agreements (Armed Services).

H.R. 10794, sponsored by Rep. Norma J. Torres (D-CA-35) — would create a grant program to help states improve access to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (Education and Workforce).

H.Con.Res. 124, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — would direct the President under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that Congress has not authorized (Foreign Affairs); Rep. Thomas Massie is listed as a cosponsor.
H.Res. 1621, sponsored by Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA-46) — would express profound sorrow over the death of Alexander Michel Odeh (Oversight and Government Reform).
H.Res. 1622, sponsored by Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24) — would express support for preserving, protecting and maintaining statues and monuments honoring Christopher Columbus (Natural Resources).
H.Res. 1623, sponsored by Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-AR-4) — would recognize October 2026 as “National Dyslexia Awareness Month” (Education and Workforce).
